source.title: DeepOBS: A Deep Learning Optimizer Benchmark Suite
source.authors: Frank Schneider; Lukas Balles; Philipp Hennig

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Table 2 is flattened in the supplied text, but its optimizer and test-problem groupings are recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: Compares SGD, momentum, and Adam on held-out performance across benchmark problems, testing whether optimizer choice affects generalization. It uses benchmark tasks and measures rather than the original studies’ experimental designs.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports test performance for three optimizers across eight problems. Rows below retain the six image-classification problems and the character-language problem relevant to V4. The quadratic problem and two VAE problems are outside V4’s stated image-classification and language-model settings. Prose says optimizer rankings differ between train and test loss on P6 and P7, but supplies no recoverable numeric values for those curves.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out comparisons of Adam, SGD and momentum SGD on four image-classification problems and one character-language problem, directly testing V4 under learning-rate-only tuning. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the relevant empirical conclusion: optimizer rankings depend on the problem and metric, and no optimizer consistently generalizes best. The paper's main contribution is the DeepOBS benchmark and evaluation protocol.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benchmark training problems and test performance, not random-label fitting or the original studies' individual benchmark designs. The study tunes learning rates on a logarithmic grid for each optimizer and problem; Adam uses default parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: The best optimizer varies by test problem; train and test loss rankings differ on P6 and P7. Adam's optimal learning rate usually falls in the 10−4 to 10−3 order of magnitude, while SGD and Momentum have a slightly larger spread.
record.problems: Ten runs per selected hyperparameter setting are averaged, but Table 2 provides no uncertainty values. Results use an exhaustive but finite learning-rate grid and only the stated benchmark tasks. The paper notes different rankings for train and test loss on P6 and P7 without tabulating those values.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded P1 Quadratic Deep, P2 MNIST VAE, and P5 F-MNIST VAE because they are not the image-classification or language benchmarks specified by V4. Table 2, P1, P2, P5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width variation beyond the interpolation threshold.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.

Decay-schedule tuning, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and the word-level language-model exception. The supplied text does not establish whether Adam's lower test accuracy occurs despite equal or better training performance.
Batch-size interventions and adaptations intended to close a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Identification and removal of memorized training examples.

missing.what: Separate training-loss and test-loss comparisons for P6 and P7. Section 4 explicitly reports differing optimizer rankings, but the supplied flattened Figure 2 does not recover optimizer-specific values or directions. Add these comparisons if recoverable; do not infer that Adam trains better from this statement alone.
missing.locator: Section 4, second observation; Figure 2, P6 and P7

record.verdict_notes: All Table 2 accuracy values in the record match the supplied text. There are four image-classification problems and one language problem, not six image-classification problems. Learning rates are selected using test accuracy or test loss on a 36-point grid, followed by ten runs at the selected setting; these are test-selected benchmark results. Adam's wins qualify V4's scope rather than contradicting its non-universal wording. No additional overall mixed-results label is needed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Convolutional and fully connected networks are not compared on the same image task.

No language benchmark comparisons with broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD; training performance is not tabulated numerically. The study tunes learning rates on a log grid and does not report tuning decay schedules.
Batch size is not varied as an intervention.
Dropout is not varied as an intervention.
Sharpness and other generalization measures are not evaluated.
Memorized examples are not identified or removed.

relation.reason: Its own image-classification and character-language results directly compare Adam with SGD and Momentum on held-out performance.

tranche.reason: The benchmark supplies independent optimizer comparisons using individually tuned learning rates and test performance, addressing V4 through a different experimental protocol.

source_check.notes: Learning rates were selected using test accuracy, or test loss when accuracy was unavailable; reported performance therefore uses the tuning metric. Table 2 reports ten-run means without uncertainty; the authors' problem-dependent conclusion is accurately summarized.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Adam has lower test performance than SGD and Momentum on CIFAR-100, SVHN, and Tolstoi CharRNN (R9, R12, R15); the authors also state Momentum is significantly better on CIFAR-100 (R8).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: With learning rates tuned on a log grid, Adam has higher test accuracy than both SGD and Momentum on these two classifiers (R3, R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors conclude there is no optimizer that universally generalizes better; results depend on the problem. Table 2 shows both Adam wins and losses (R3, R6, R9, R12, R15).
